mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 320si engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 320si engine replacement typically costs £2,500-£4,500 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, or £3,500-£6,000 fitted by a specialist. Used engines start from around £1,200-£2,500, while reconditioned units range from £2,200 to £3,500.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 320si engine and a standard 320i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 320si uses a completely unique N45B20A engine, not an evolution of the standard 320i's N46 or N43. Differences include: increased bore (85mm vs 84mm) and shortened stroke (88mm vs 90mm); higher 11.0:1 compression ratio; larger valves and wilder camshafts; no Valvetronic system; aluminium alloy cylinder liners; hand-built construction; and a carbon fibre cam cover saving 10kg.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a standard 320i engine in my 320si?

acceptedAnswer.text: No - a standard 320i engine (N46 or N43) is not a direct replacement for the 320si's N45B20A. The engines have different bore and stroke dimensions, different cylinder heads, different engine management, and different ancillaries. Fitting a non-original engine will also significantly reduce the car's collector value.

mainEntity.name: Why are 320si engines so expensive and hard to find?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only 2,600 320si examples were built worldwide, with just 500 right-hand drive cars for the UK. The engines were hand-built at BMW's Hams Hall plant alongside racing engines. BMW main dealers have quoted 10-month waits for new engines. Parts supply is extremely limited, and many components are unique to this engine.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 320si engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 3 Series 320si engine replacement takes 2-4 days for a specialist workshop, assuming the replacement engine is available. However, sourcing the correct N45B20A engine can take significantly longer due to rarity.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 320si replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt and reconditioned BMW 3 Series 320si engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with a shorter warranty (30-90 days) depending on the supplier - always confirm exact terms before purchasing.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 320si - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 320si was a homologation special produced to meet FIA World Touring Car Championship (WTCC) and Super 2000 regulations. Just 2,600 examples were built worldwide between late 2005 and mid-2006, of which only 500 were right-hand drive for the UK market. Based on the E90 320i M Sport, the 320si received a completely re-engineered four-cylinder engine - the N45B20A - which was hand-built alongside BMW's racing engines at the Hams Hall plant.

milestones.description: September 2005 - August 2006 - N45B20A, 2.0-litre 16-valve DOHC, 173hp, hand-built homologation engine

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 3 Series 320si is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.h4: Engine Failure & Parts Scarcity - Why the BMW 3 Series 320si is a Specialist Proposition
problems.typicalFailureMileage: Highly variable - many fail due to age-related issues or low-mileage use
problems.rootCause: The N45B20A is a completely unique engine, not an evolution of the standard 320i's N46B20. It features different bore and stroke dimensions (85mm x 88mm), wilder camshafts, bigger valves, a higher 11.0:1 compression ratio, and crucially - no Valvetronic system. The engine was hand-built and shares components with racing units. Parts are extremely difficult to source; BMW main dealers have quoted 10-month waits for new engines.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 320si is worth approximately £4,000-£12,000 depending on condition and mileage. Well-preserved examples can command significantly more due to the car's rarity and homologation special status. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: a used engine or specialist rebuild may still be viable due to the car's future classic potential. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car as a long-term investment. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£12,000+: replacement cost is typically justified by the car's rarity and collector appeal.
problems.recommendation: If your 320si has developed running issues, start with specialist diagnostics - many idle and cold-start problems are software-related rather than mechanical. If the engine has suffered catastrophic failure, a used or rebuilt N45B20A is the only correct option - a standard 320i engine is not compatible and will destroy the car's value. Given the rarity of the 320si, investing in the correct engine is almost always the right decision for a genuine example.
